question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She had a ______ for creating beautiful artwork.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. talent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Talent" means a natural aptitude or skill for doing something well. The fixed expression is "to have a talent for something". (प्रतिभा / हुनर)

◦ Correct: She had a talent for creating beautiful artwork.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mode" (a way or manner of doing something), Option 2 "post" (a job/position or a pole) and Option 3 "trigger" (something that sets off an action) do not collocate with "for creating beautiful artwork".

• Note the preposition: we say "a talent for" (a talent for music, a talent for painting), never "a talent of".

NOTE

• Synonyms of talent: gift, flair, knack, aptitude, genius. Related idiom: "a gifted artist" = an artist with natural talent.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase.

Reading between the lines
option_1: Understanding a deeper or hidden meaning
option_2: Avoiding reading and engaging in gossips
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Understanding a deeper or hidden meaning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "reading between the lines" means understanding the hidden or implied meaning of something that is not stated directly. (छिपे हुए अर्थ को समझना)

◦ Example: If you read between the lines of her letter, you can see she is unhappy with the decision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Taking things literally" is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Options 2 and 4 take the words literally and miss the idiomatic sense.

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "get the drift", "take the hint", "the subtext". Idioms must never be interpreted word-for-word — they carry a figurative meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Meticulous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Precise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; very careful and exact. Its closest synonym is "precise" (accurate and exact). (अति सावधान / सूक्ष्मता से काम करने वाला)

◦ Example: The meticulous/precise accountant checked every entry twice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Negligent" (careless, failing to take proper care) and Option 3 "Careless" are antonyms of meticulous.

• Option 4 "Random" (without a plan or pattern) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of meticulous: precise, careful, thorough, painstaking, scrupulous, fastidious. Antonyms: careless, negligent, sloppy, slapdash.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The sudden plot twist in the story added an element of __________ that kept readers on the edge of their seats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ambiguity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ambiguity" means uncertainty; the quality of being open to more than one interpretation. A sudden plot twist creates uncertainty (ambiguity), which keeps readers "on the edge of their seats" (excited and in suspense). (अनिश्चितता / अस्पष्टता)

◦ Correct: The sudden plot twist added an element of ambiguity that kept readers on the edge of their seats.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "redundancy" (unnecessary repetition), Option 3 "monotony" (dull sameness) and Option 4 "predictability" (being easy to foresee) would make the story boring — the opposite of keeping readers in suspense.

• The idiom "on the edge of one's seat" means very excited and giving full attention because of suspense.

NOTE

• Word family: ambiguous (adjective), ambiguity (noun), ambiguously (adverb). Synonyms: vagueness, uncertainty, obscurity. Antonyms: clarity, certainty.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The soldiers / sacrifice their lives / to guarding / the nation and its boundaries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to guarding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "to" used as part of the infinitive of purpose, the base form of the verb (V1) is required — "to guard", not "to guarding".

◦ Correct: The soldiers sacrifice their lives to guard the nation and its boundaries.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The soldiers", "sacrifice their lives" and "the nation and its boundaries" are all grammatically correct.

• "To + V-ing" is correct only when "to" is a preposition in fixed expressions like "look forward to seeing", "used to going", "committed to serving". Here "to" expresses purpose, so the infinitive "to guard" is needed.

NOTE

• Infinitive of purpose: "He works hard to earn money", "She came to help us". Purpose can also be expressed as "in order to + V1" or "so as to + V1".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Eficcient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eficcient" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Efficient", meaning working well without wasting time, money or energy. (कार्यकुशल / दक्ष)

◦ Example: She is an efficient manager who completes every task on time.

• Spelling key: EF + FI + CIENT — double "f", single "c" before "-ient".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Belligerent" (hostile, aggressive), "Tournament" (a sports competition) and "Parliament" (the supreme legislative body) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Word family: efficient (adjective), efficiency (noun), efficiently (adverb). Similar "-cient" words: sufficient, deficient, proficient, ancient.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

One who is a newcomer
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Neophyte.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Neophyte" is a person who is new to a subject, skill, activity or belief; a beginner or newcomer. (नौसिखिया / नवागंतुक)

◦ Example: As a neophyte in politics, he made several early mistakes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Polyglot" — one who knows or speaks many languages.

• Option 3 "Narcissist" — one who has excessive love/admiration for oneself.

• Option 4 "Nepotist" — one who shows favouritism to relatives, especially in giving jobs.

NOTE

• Words meaning beginner: neophyte, novice, tyro, amateur, rookie, greenhorn. Antonym: veteran, expert.

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets.

The teacher commended the student for his (diligent) efforts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Lazy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligent" means hardworking; showing steady, careful and persistent effort. Its antonym is "lazy", meaning unwilling to work or use energy. (परिश्रमी का विलोम — आलसी)

◦ Example: A diligent student studies daily, while a lazy one avoids work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Hardworking", 3 "Industrious" and 4 "Conscientious" are all synonyms of diligent, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diligent: industrious, assiduous, sedulous, painstaking, conscientious. Antonyms: lazy, idle, indolent, slothful, lethargic.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

She is an epitome of grace.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Example.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Epitome" means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality or type. Its closest synonym is "example". (आदर्श उदाहरण / प्रतिमूर्ति)

◦ Example: She is an epitome/perfect example of grace — she embodies gracefulness completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Admirer" (one who admires), Option 3 "Believer" (one who believes) and Option 4 "Destroyer" (one who destroys) are unrelated to the meaning of epitome.

• Pronunciation note: epitome is pronounced "i-PIT-uh-mee" (four syllables).

NOTE

• Synonyms of epitome: embodiment, personification, quintessence, exemplar, model. "The epitome of ..." is a common construction: the epitome of elegance/honesty/luxury.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The dog / eager wagged / its tail when / it saw its owner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. eager wagged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A verb ("wagged") must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Eager" is an adjective; the adverb "eagerly" is required.

◦ Correct: The dog eagerly wagged its tail when it saw its owner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The dog", "its tail when" and "it saw its owner" are all grammatically correct.

• Note the correct use of "its" (possessive) here — not "it's" (contraction of "it is").

NOTE

• Adjectives describe nouns (an eager dog); adverbs describe verbs, adjectives or other adverbs (wagged eagerly). Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding "-ly": eager → eagerly, quick → quickly, happy → happily.

question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Roma was the dearest child of her parents.
option_1: At sixes and sevens with her parents
option_2: The apple of her parents’ eyes
option_3: The star of her parents’ eyes
option_4: The body and soul of her parents
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The apple of her parents’ eyes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the apple of one's eye" means a person who is loved most dearly; a favourite. It correctly substitutes "the dearest child". (आँखों का तारा / अत्यंत प्रिय)

◦ Correct: Roma was the apple of her parents' eyes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "at sixes and sevens" means in a state of confusion or disorder — it does not fit.

• Options 3 "the star of her parents' eyes" and 4 "the body and soul of her parents" are not standard English idioms.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of affection: "the blue-eyed boy" (a favourite person), "hold someone dear", "dote on someone". "At sixes and sevens" (confused) is a frequently asked SSC idiom — do not confuse the two.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
option_1: The librarian told the childern to return their books by Fryday.
option_2: The librarian told the children to return their books by Friday.
option_3: The libraian told the childrean to return their books by Friday.
option_4: The liberian told the childrean to return their boooks by Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The librarian told the children to return their books by Friday.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "librarian" (LIBRAR + IAN), "children" (irregular plural of child) and "Friday" (FRI + DAY).

◦ Correct: The librarian told the children to return their books by Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "children" as "childern" and "Friday" as "Fryday".

• Option 3 misspells "librarian" as "libraian" and "children" as "childrean".

• Option 4 misspells "librarian" as "liberian", "children" as "childrean" and "books" as "boooks".

NOTE

• "Librarian" = a person in charge of a library (library + -an). Irregular plurals to remember: child → children, ox → oxen, man → men, foot → feet. Days of the week always begin with a capital letter.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The ________(sarcastic) comments by her husband made her feel uncomfortable, and she decided to walk out of the relationship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gracious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sarcastic" means mocking, taunting or using bitter irony to hurt someone. Its antonym is "gracious", meaning kind, polite and courteous. (व्यंग्यात्मक का विलोम — विनम्र/शालीन)

◦ Sense: The gracious comments would be the opposite of hurtful, sarcastic remarks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "ruinous" (causing destruction) and Option 3 "ambiguous" (unclear) are unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4 "harmonious" (free from conflict) usually describes relationships or sounds, not individual comments, and is not the direct antonym of sarcastic.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sarcastic: mocking, caustic, satirical, ironical, scornful. Antonyms: gracious, polite, courteous, complimentary, kind.

question:
Change the following into superlative degree.

She is taller than other girls in the class.
option_1: No other girl in the class is as tall as she.
option_2: In the class she is taller than other girls.
option_3: She is tall girl in the class.
option_4: She is the tallest girl in the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She is the tallest girl in the class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The superlative degree compares one person/thing with all others in a group and takes the structure "the + superlative adjective". The superlative of "tall" is "tallest".

◦ Correct: She is the tallest girl in the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No other girl in the class is as tall as she" is the positive degree form of the same idea, not the superlative.

• Option 2 keeps the comparative degree ("taller than").

• Option 3 "She is tall girl in the class" is grammatically incomplete (missing article and degree).

NOTE

• Degree transformation of the same idea: Positive — "No other girl in the class is as tall as she." Comparative — "She is taller than any other girl in the class." Superlative — "She is the tallest girl in the class." The superlative always takes the article "the".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The 100-year-old banyan was blown off in the storm last night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was blown off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For a tree being knocked to the ground by wind, the correct phrasal verb is "blow down" (or "blow over"), not "blow off". "Blow off" means to be carried away off a surface (e.g., a hat blown off one's head).

◦ Correct: The 100-year-old banyan was blown down in the storm last night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "The 100-year-old banyan", "in the storm" and "last night" are all correct.

• When a compound adjective with a number precedes a noun, the noun in it stays singular with hyphens: "a 100-year-old banyan" (not "100-years-old") — this part is correctly framed.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "blow": blow down (fall by wind), blow off (be carried off a surface), blow up (explode/inflate), blow out (extinguish), blow over (pass without harm).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

According to Mr. Sharma / the news have come / as another blow / to the family members.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the news have come.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "News" is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb, even though it ends in "-s". So it must be "the news has come", not "have come".

◦ Correct: According to Mr. Sharma, the news has come as another blow to the family members.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "According to Mr. Sharma", "as another blow" and "to the family members" are all correct.

• The idiom "come as a blow" means to be a shock or disappointment.

NOTE

• Nouns that look plural but take a singular verb: news, physics, mathematics, economics, politics, measles, innings. E.g., "No news is good news."

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

Majority of communication satelites are placed in geostationary orbits around the earth, which means that their speed matches the rate of its rotation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Satelites.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Satelites" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "satellites" — with a double 'l' and single 't' in the middle. A satellite is an object that orbits a planet. (उपग्रह)

• Spelling key: SAT + EL + LITE + S (satellite → sat-e-llite).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Communication", "rotation" and "geostationary" are all correctly spelt.

• A geostationary orbit is about 36,000 km above the equator, where a satellite's period matches the Earth's rotation (24 hours), so it appears fixed over one point.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt science words in SSC exams: satellite, parallel, laboratory, phenomenon, oxygen, environment. Remember: satellite = one "t" then double "l".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The speaker delivered an engaging speech that inspired the audience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. captivating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Engaging" means charming, attractive and holding one's attention. Its closest synonym is "captivating" (capable of attracting and holding interest). (आकर्षक / मनमोहक)

◦ Example: The engaging/captivating speech held the audience spellbound.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dreary" (dull and gloomy) is an antonym of engaging.

• Option 2 "important" and Option 4 "unnecessary" do not convey the sense of holding attention.

NOTE

• Synonyms of engaging: captivating, charming, appealing, fascinating, enchanting, absorbing. Antonyms: boring, dull, dreary, tedious.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The teacher called up the class due to the sudden snowstorm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. called off the class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "call off" means to cancel. A class cancelled because of a snowstorm is "called off". (रद्द करना)

◦ Correct: The teacher called off the class due to the sudden snowstorm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Call up" = to telephone someone / to summon for military service.

• "Call out" = to shout / to summon help (call out the army).

• "Call on" = to visit someone briefly / to appeal to someone.

• "Call in" = to ask someone to come (call in a doctor).

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "call" are repeatedly asked in SSC exams: call off (cancel), call on (visit), call up (telephone/recall), call for (demand/require), call out (shout), call in (summon).

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

Meerut is farthest from Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. far.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• No comparison with other places is being made in the sentence; it simply states distance. Hence the positive degree "far" is required — "Meerut is far from Delhi."

◦ Correct: Meerut is far from Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Farthest" (superlative) needs a defined group and the article "the" (the farthest of all the cities); it is wrong here.

• Option 1 "farther" (comparative) needs "than" for comparison.

• Options 3 "more farther" and 4 "most farthest" are double comparatives/superlatives — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "far": far – farther/further – farthest/furthest. "Farther" is used for physical distance; "further" also means "additional" (further information). Never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est" forms.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. her.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a possessive adjective (determiner) before the noun "husband". Since the subject is "Ms Navalnaya" (a single woman), the correct possessive adjective is "her".

◦ Correct: ... has always been a crucial supporter of her husband ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "their" is a plural possessive and does not agree with the singular "Ms Navalnaya".

• Option 3 "hers" is a possessive pronoun — it stands alone and cannot be used before a noun (e.g., "The book is hers").

• Option 4 "them" is an object pronoun, not a possessive.

NOTE

• Possessive adjectives (before a noun): my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Possessive pronouns (stand alone): mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. urgent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context says he "was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent" — poisoning is a life-threatening emergency, so he was taken out of Russia for "urgent treatment" (treatment needed immediately). (तत्काल / अत्यावश्यक)

◦ Correct: ... instrumental in getting him out of Russia for urgent treatment when he was poisoned ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "slow" contradicts the emergency of poisoning.

• Options 2 "crazy" and 4 "interesting" are illogical descriptions of medical treatment in this context.

NOTE

• "Urgent" collocates naturally with treatment/attention/care/need. Synonyms: immediate, pressing, critical, emergency. Antonyms: minor, trivial, non-urgent.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. described.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Described as" means called/portrayed as; referred to as. The passage says she has been "described as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition" — i.e., people refer to her by that title. (वर्णित / कहा गया)

◦ Correct: She has been described as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "detected" (discovered/noticed), Option 3 "deleted" (removed) and Option 4 "changed" (altered) do not fit the structure "been ______ as + title".

• The passive structure "be described as + noun" is a fixed pattern: "He is described as a genius."

NOTE

• Verbs that take "as" in the passive: described as, known as, regarded as, referred to as, hailed as, dubbed as. All mean giving someone a name/label.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes something that started in the past and is still true, so the present perfect passive "has been seen" is correct. The subject "Their very public love story and family life" is treated as one combined idea, taking "has".

◦ Correct: Their very public love story and family life ... has been seen as an inspiration for their supporters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is been" and Option 4 "will been" are grammatically impossible combinations ("is/will" cannot be followed directly by "been").

• Option 3 "was being seen" (past continuous passive) wrongly limits the sense to a temporary past action.

NOTE

• Present perfect passive = has/have + been + V3 (has been seen, has been described). It is used for actions completed in the past whose effect continues in the present.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. gave up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "give up" means to quit or abandon something. She "gave up her job" (quit her banking career) to bring up their two children. (छोड़ देना / त्याग देना)

◦ Correct: ... she had a career in banking but gave up her job to bring up their two children ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "keep back" (to withhold) is also in the wrong tense — the past tense is needed after "had a career ... but".

• Option 2 "broke down" (stopped working / lost control emotionally) and Option 4 "brought about" (caused to happen) do not fit "her job".

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "give": give up (quit), give in (surrender), give away (donate/reveal), give out (distribute/come to an end), give off (emit). Also note "bring up" in the passage = to raise/rear children.

question: Who among the following is the author of the autobiography 'Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography" (2017) is the autobiography of the celebrated Indian author of British descent, Ruskin Bond. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond lives in Landour, Mussoorie (Uttarakhand). His famous works include The Room on the Roof (which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize), The Blue Umbrella, A Flight of Pigeons and Rusty stories.

• He received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992), the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

NOTE

• Famous autobiographies: Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Truth, Love and a Little Malice (Khushwant Singh).

question: In which of the following years did the battle of Plassey take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1757.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the English East India Company under Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal. (प्लासी का युद्ध — 1757)

• The Nawab was defeated mainly because of the treachery of his commander Mir Jafar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• After the battle, Mir Jafar was made the Nawab of Bengal, and the battle laid the foundation of British rule in India.

• Plassey (Palashi) is situated on the banks of the river Bhagirathi/Hooghly in West Bengal.

NOTE

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) — the Company under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II; it was followed by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), which gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

question: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a legendary exponent of the Kuchipudi classical dance, famous for his female impersonation roles, especially Satyabhama in the dance-drama "Bhama Kalapam". (कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village of Kuchipudi in the Krishna district; Siddhendra Yogi is regarded as its founder.

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma received the Padma Shri (1970) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam — Kerala; Odissi — Odisha; Kathak — Uttar Pradesh; Manipuri — Manipur; Sattriya — Assam.

question: _________ was/were the mascot(s) of the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Juhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Juhi" was the official mascot of the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2023, held in Ranchi, Jharkhand. (जूही — शुभंकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India won the Women's Asian Champions Trophy 2023, defeating Japan 4-0 in the final at Ranchi.

• Hockey India organised the tournament at the Marang Gomke Jaipal Singh Munda Astroturf Hockey Stadium.

NOTE

• Famous sports mascots: Appu (elephant — 1982 Asian Games, Delhi), Sheera (tiger — 2010 Commonwealth Games, Delhi), Miraitowa (Tokyo 2020 Olympics), Phryge (Paris 2024 Olympics).

question: Sanchi stupa was rediscovered in the year ________ by General Henry Taylor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1818.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh) was rediscovered in 1818 by General Henry Taylor, a British officer, after it had lain abandoned and covered by vegetation for centuries. (साँची स्तूप — 1818)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka (Maurya dynasty) in the 3rd century BCE; its famous gateways (toranas) were added later under the Satavahanas.

• Sanchi is situated in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, near Bhopal, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1989).

NOTE

• A stupa is a hemispherical Buddhist structure containing relics. Other famous stupas: Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh), Bharhut (Madhya Pradesh), Dhamek (Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh).

question: In November 2023, who was appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heeralal Samariya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Heeralal Samariya was appointed (and sworn in by President Droupadi Murmu) as the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) of India. He became the first person from the Dalit community to head the Central Information Commission. (हीरालाल सामरिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005.

• The CIC is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

NOTE

• The RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 empowered the Central Government to prescribe the tenure and salary of Information Commissioners (tenure now 3 years). The first CIC of India was Wajahat Habibullah.

question: Stunted growth, which is common in children growing up in extreme poverty, is a sure sign of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Undernutrition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Stunted growth (low height-for-age) in children is a sure sign of undernutrition — chronic deficiency of energy, proteins and micronutrients in the diet. (अल्पपोषण / कुपोषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Forms of child undernutrition: stunting (low height-for-age), wasting (low weight-for-height) and underweight (low weight-for-age).

• Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) and marasmus (protein-energy deficiency) are severe forms of malnutrition in children.

• Government initiatives against malnutrition: POSHAN Abhiyan (National Nutrition Mission, 2018), Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN) and ICDS/Anganwadi services.

NOTE

• The Global Hunger Index uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality as its indicators.

question: Which Indian actress from the following, is also a popular dancer and received the Smita Patil Memorial award for her role in the movie Damini?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meenakshi Seshadri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meenakshi Seshadri, an Indian actress and a trained classical dancer (Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi and Odissi), received the Smita Patil Memorial Award for her acclaimed role in the movie Damini (1993). (मीनाक्षी शेषाद्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Damini (1993), directed by Rajkumar Santoshi, dealt with a woman's fight for justice; Sunny Deol won a National Film Award (Special Jury) and Filmfare for the same film.

• The Smita Patil Memorial Award is given in memory of the celebrated actress Smita Patil, known for her contribution to parallel cinema.

NOTE

• Meenakshi Seshadri won the Miss India title in 1981 at the age of 17, one of the youngest ever winners.

question: In which of the following cities was the headquarters of Theosophical Society established in British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adyar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The international headquarters of the Theosophical Society was established at Adyar (Madras/Chennai) in 1882. (अड्यार — थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Theosophical Society was founded in New York (USA) in 1875 by Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel H. S. Olcott; they moved to India in 1879.

• Annie Besant became its president in 1907; she also founded the Central Hindu College at Banaras (1898), started the Home Rule League (1916) and became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (Calcutta session, 1917).

NOTE

• The society promoted the study of ancient religions and philosophy (Upanishads, Vedanta) and the ideas of universal brotherhood, karma and rebirth.

question: If the server manages to land a legal serve and the receiver is unable to return the ball, it is known as an ace and the server gets the point. Which of the following sport is referred here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, an "ace" is a legal serve that the receiver fails to touch or return, winning the server the point directly. (टेनिस — 'ऐस')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tennis terms: love (0), deuce (40-40), advantage, fault, double fault, let, tie-break, volley, smash, lob.

• The four Grand Slam tournaments: Australian Open (hard court), French Open/Roland Garros (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and US Open (hard court).

NOTE

• Famous Indian tennis players: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna, Sumit Nagal. Wrestling, boxing and shooting have no "serve", so the description fits only tennis.

question: At which of the following places is the Lalbagh Flower Show organised, where thousands of flower varieties are put on display in different forms with a particular theme (which changes every year) during the exhibition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Lalbagh Flower Show is organised at the Lalbagh Botanical Garden in Bengaluru (Karnataka), twice a year — on Republic Day and Independence Day — with a new theme each time. (लालबाग पुष्प प्रदर्शनी — बेंगलुरु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lalbagh Botanical Garden was commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760 and completed by his son Tipu Sultan.

• The garden houses the Glass House (modelled on London's Crystal Palace), where the flower show is held, and a famous rock formation (Lalbagh Rock) about 3,000 million years old.

NOTE

• Bengaluru is known as the "Garden City of India" and also the "Silicon Valley of India".

question: According to Census of India 2011, which is the largest religious community in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Hindus form the largest religious community, constituting about 79.8% of the total population. (हिंदू — 79.8%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Religious composition (Census 2011): Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India (7th after Independence); its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". The Census Commissioner was C. Chandramouli.

NOTE

• The first Census in India was conducted in 1872 (under Lord Mayo); a regular decennial (every 10 years) census began in 1881 (under Lord Ripon).

question: The Narora ________ Power Station is located in Uttar Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS) is a nuclear power plant located at Narora, Bulandshahr district, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Ganga. (नरोरा परमाणु विद्युत केंद्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Narora has two Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) of 220 MW each, operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

• Major nuclear power stations in India: Tarapur (Maharashtra — the first, 1969), Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu), Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu — largest), Kaiga (Karnataka), Kakrapar (Gujarat), Narora (UP).

NOTE

• India's nuclear programme is based on the three-stage plan of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha, the father of India's nuclear programme; the Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948.

question: Which of the following Union Territories of India marks the lowest poverty in National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023 (released by NITI Aayog), among the Union Territories, Puducherry recorded the lowest proportion of multidimensionally poor population. (पुडुचेरी — न्यूनतम बहुआयामी गरीबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The MPI measures deprivations across three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — using 12 indicators (e.g., nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, sanitation, housing, bank accounts).

• As per the 2023 review, about 13.5 crore Indians escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21; Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya and UP showed high poverty levels, while Kerala, Goa and Delhi were among the lowest.

NOTE

• The National MPI is prepared by NITI Aayog with technical support from UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative).

question: To which of the following classes of compounds does cyclohexane belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alicyclic compound.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) is an alicyclic compound — a carbocyclic (ring) compound that behaves like an aliphatic (open-chain) compound and is not aromatic. (एलिसाइक्लिक यौगिक)

• It is a saturated ring of six carbon atoms with only single bonds (a cycloalkane).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Benzenoid aromatic compounds contain a benzene ring (e.g., benzene, toluene, naphthalene).

• Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds are aromatic but lack a benzene ring (e.g., tropolone, azulene).

• Heterocyclic compounds have at least one non-carbon atom (N, O, S) in the ring (e.g., pyridine, furan, thiophene).

NOTE

• Aromaticity requires a planar ring with delocalised π-electrons obeying Hückel's rule (4n + 2 π electrons). Cyclohexane has no π-electrons, hence it is non-aromatic (alicyclic).

question: Groundwater is an important source of water. The top level of the groundwater layer is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is water table.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The upper level/surface of the groundwater (the level below which the ground is saturated with water) is called the "water table". (भौम जल स्तर / वाटर टेबल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The water-saturated layer of rock/soil below the water table that yields water is called an aquifer.

• The process by which rainwater seeps down through the soil to recharge groundwater is called infiltration; deliberate recharging is rainwater harvesting.

• Over-extraction through tube wells and pumps causes depletion of the water table.

NOTE

• "Sea level" is the mean level of the ocean surface; a "well" is a man-made structure to draw groundwater — neither is the top level of groundwater itself.

question: Women's Reservation Bill 2023 [The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023] was introduced in Lok Sabha on __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19 Sep 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Women's Reservation Bill 2023 — The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023, named the "Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam" — was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 19 September 2023, the first day of business in the new Parliament building. (नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम — 19 सितंबर 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Bill provides 33% (one-third) reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including seats reserved for SCs/STs.

• It was passed by the Lok Sabha on 20 September and by the Rajya Sabha on 21 September 2023, and became the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

• The reservation will come into effect after the first census and delimitation conducted after the Act's commencement, and will continue for 15 years.

NOTE

• It was introduced by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. Women already have reservation (at least one-third, many states 50%) in Panchayati Raj institutions under the 73rd/74th Amendments (1992).

question: Which of the following Parts of the Indian Constitution mentions about the relations between the Union and the States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part XI.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part XI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 245 to 263) deals with the relations between the Union and the States — both legislative relations (Articles 245–255) and administrative relations (Articles 256–263). (भाग XI — केंद्र-राज्य संबंध)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Financial relations between the Centre and the States are covered in Part XII (Articles 268–293).

• Part VIII — Union Territories; Part X — Scheduled and Tribal Areas; Part VII (dealing with Part B states) was repealed by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

• The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

NOTE

• Commissions on Centre–State relations: Sarkaria Commission (1983) and Punchhi Commission (2007).

question: Where of the following was Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s Home Rule Movement active?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded his Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum (Poona session), and it was active in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. (बाल गंगाधर तिलक — होम रूल लीग, महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Annie Besant started her own Home Rule League in September 1916 at Adyar (Madras), covering the rest of India.

• The movement demanded self-government (Home Rule) for India within the British Empire, on the lines of the Irish Home Rule movement.

• Tilak gave the famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it".

NOTE

• Tilak was called "Lokmanya"; he started the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) and wrote "Gita Rahasya". Valentine Chirol called him the "Father of Indian Unrest".

question: When did Bindusara ascend the Maurya throne?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 297 BCE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, ascended the Maurya throne in 297 BCE and ruled up to about 273 BCE. (बिंदुसार — 297 ईसा पूर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bindusara was known to the Greeks as "Amitrochates" (Sanskrit Amitraghata — "slayer of enemies").

• The Greek ambassador Deimachus was sent to his court by Antiochus I of Syria. Bindusara followed the Ajivika sect.

• He was succeeded by his son Ashoka the Great (c. 273/268 BCE), who fought the Kalinga War (261 BCE).

NOTE

• Maurya dynasty order: Chandragupta Maurya (321–297 BCE) → Bindusara (297–273 BCE) → Ashoka. The dynasty was founded with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

question: Which of the following is NOT a service of micro finance institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micro deposit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) provide financial services to low-income households, chiefly micro loans (micro credit), micro savings and micro insurance. "Micro deposit" is not a standard service category of MFIs. (माइक्रो डिपॉज़िट — माइक्रोफाइनेंस सेवा नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Microfinance provides small collateral-free loans to the poor, self-help groups (SHGs) and micro-entrepreneurs who lack access to formal banking.

• The concept was popularised by Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Nobel Peace Prize, 2006).

• In India, the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was started by NABARD (1992); the MUDRA scheme (2015) funds micro-enterprises (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun loans).

NOTE

• MFIs in India are regulated by the RBI (NBFC-MFIs). Small Finance Banks (e.g., Bandhan, Ujjivan) evolved from microfinance institutions.

question: Which Hindustani classical musician is credited with popularising the Sarangi as a solo classical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ram Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ram Narayan is credited with popularising the "Sarangi" — a bowed string instrument — as a solo classical instrument in Hindustani music, taking it beyond its traditional accompaniment role. (पंडित राम नारायण — सारंगी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2005); the sarangi is said to be the instrument closest to the human voice.

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar maestro (Bharat Ratna, 1999); Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma — popularised the santoor; Pandit Jnan Prakash Ghosh — noted tabla player and harmonium exponent.

NOTE

• Instruments and maestros: Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan; Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan; Flute — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain; Violin — Dr. N. Rajam.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the promotion of international peace and security?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51 (a Directive Principle of State Policy) directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. (अनुच्छेद 51 — अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 44 — Uniform Civil Code for citizens.

• Article 47 — duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living and to improve public health (prohibition of intoxicating drinks/drugs).

• Article 49 — protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance.

NOTE

• The Directive Principles (Part IV, Articles 36–51) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution; they are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country (Article 37).

question: The ‘Mangla’ oil field is located in which district of Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barmer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mangla" oil field is located in the Barmer district of Rajasthan. It was discovered in 2004 and is one of the largest onshore oil discoveries in India in recent decades. (मंगला तेल क्षेत्र — बाड़मेर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Mangla, Bhagyam and Aishwariya (MBA) fields of the Barmer basin are operated by Cairn Oil & Gas (Vedanta Ltd).

• Crude from Mangla is transported through a continuously heated pipeline (Barmer to Bhogat, Gujarat) — one of the world's longest heated pipelines.

• A major refinery-cum-petrochemical complex (HPCL Rajasthan Refinery) is coming up at Pachpadra, Barmer.

NOTE

• Other Indian oil fields: Digboi (Assam — oldest), Bombay High (offshore, Maharashtra), Ankleshwar & Kalol (Gujarat), Ravva (KG basin).

question: By what name is the species of Scaphopoda Mollusca 'Dentalium' commonly known?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tusk shells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dentalium", a genus of the class Scaphopoda (phylum Mollusca), is commonly known as the "tusk shell" (or tooth shell) because its long, curved, tapering shell resembles a miniature elephant's tusk. (टस्क शेल — हाथीदांत जैसा कवच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Scaphopods are marine molluscs that live buried in sand/mud and feed using thread-like tentacles called captacula.

• Classes of Mollusca: Gastropoda (snails), Bivalvia/Pelecypoda (clams, mussels), Cephalopoda ("head-foot" — octopus, squid), Scaphopoda (tusk shells), Polyplacophora (chitons).

NOTE

• Mollusca is the second-largest animal phylum; molluscs have a soft body, mantle and usually a calcareous shell. Pearls are produced by the bivalve Pinctada (pearl oyster).
